name: nutrition-demo
narrative: Priya runs a child-nutrition program funded to deliver RUTF and screen for malnutrition through three network managers — Amara in the Northern Cluster, Bakary in Central, and Chidi in the Eastern. Monday morning she opens the Program Admin Report and reads all three managers' last four weekly reviews as one grid: Northern is meeting the SOP across the board, while Central and Eastern both read below it. She clicks a resolved week in Central's row and an inline panel names the worker who was flagged and links the audit and coaching task that dealt with it. She opens the run behind the cell and reads the same per-worker review Bakary worked from, its buttons now reporting what was done, then opens the flagged worker's audit and sees the child's MUAC photos the auditor passed with her own eyes. She reads the closed coaching conversation and watches that worker's screening numbers recover week over week. Then she turns to the harder cells — Central's still-open investigation, where the coaching is paused mid-exchange, and Eastern's case where the AI image review caught misleading MUAC photos and the worker was suspended. She lands back on the aggregate column and decides for herself which network manager needs her this week. And to see what all that oversight is ultimately for, she opens one flagged child's follow-up timeline and watches the child's MUAC climb visit by visit — from a severe-acute red reading up through yellow into green, recovered — the program-to-child line closing on a child getting better.

priya.name: Priya Sharma
priya.intro: Priya runs a child-nutrition program through three network managers and their frontline teams across the Northern, Central, and Eastern clusters. She needs to know — without reading a dozen separate weekly reviews — which network manager is on top of the MUAC screening SOP and which flagged workers still need attention.

slides.title: Priya sees the whole program at a glance
slides.narration: The completed Program Admin Report: three cluster rows (Northern, Central, Eastern) by four week columns, plus the Window aggregate column on the right. Each ran week is a card with a status pill and Flagged/Audits/Tasks counts; the aggregate carries each manager's SOP MET or BELOW verdict.

slides.title: Priya clicks into a resolved week in Central's row
slides.narration: Clicking the 'All resolved' week cell in the Central Cluster row opens the inline run-detail panel beneath the row: the flagged worker Kadi Fofana sorted first, with her flag label and links to the exact audit and coaching task, each showing its resolved outcome.

slides.title: Priya opens the run behind the cell
slides.narration: Bakary's underlying weekly nutrition review: the per-worker table with MUAC distribution, SAM/MAM rates and gender split, flag pills on Kadi's row, and a state-aware Actions column where her buttons read 'View Audit' and 'View Task' because those records now exist.

slides.title: Priya checks the child's MUAC photos the auditor saw
slides.narration: The audit page for the flagged worker: the assessment-count header and the MUAC photo thumbnails, each labeled with its per-photo decision, with the audit's overall verdict — the individual children's evidence behind the flag.

slides.title: Priya reads the coaching that turned the numbers around
slides.narration: The closed coaching task for Kadi Fofana: the Closed status with its outcome, and below it the Coaching Conversation panel with the full bot/worker exchange — the manager's route-plan coaching, then the follow-up week where the screening profile came back to the area's expected picture with referrals into treatment.

slides.title: Now the harder case — Central's still-open week
slides.narration: Back on the report, the open-work cell in Central's row. Clicking it opens the detail panel naming Lola Kargbo with an in-review audit and a still-open coaching task, distinct from the resolved case Priya just closed out.

slides.title: Priya inspects the audit still in review
slides.narration: The in-review audit page for Lola Kargbo: MUAC photo cards in mixed states — decided ones carrying their badges, the rest undecided — and the action button reading 'Save Progress' because the review is not finished.

slides.title: Priya checks on the coaching mid-conversation
slides.narration: The investigating task page for Lola Kargbo: the task still open with its Close Task action available, and the Coaching Conversation panel showing the opening messages of an unfinished exchange about reaching the far compounds.

slides.title: The third manager — an AI-caught misleading-photo case
slides.narration: Eastern Cluster's flagged week cell. Clicking it opens the detail panel naming Vida Kargbo with a suspended-outcome coaching task, the case the AI image review flagged for misleading MUAC photos — visibly distinct from Central's resolved and open cases.

slides.title: Priya opens the audit and sees what the AI flagged
slides.narration: Vida Kargbo's audit page: the reviewed MUAC photos, each flagged photo carrying the AI reviewer's "Hyperzoomed" badge, and the overall Fail verdict — the AI-review evidence the auditor confirmed before the coaching task closed as a suspension.

slides.title: Priya returns to the aggregate and makes her call
slides.narration: The Program Admin Report with the Window aggregate column in frame: Northern carrying its SOP MET pill, Central and Eastern their BELOW pills, each with runs completed, flag totals, and outcome counts side by side — the contrast that decides where Priya spends her week.

slides.title: Priya follows one child's recovery
slides.narration: The SAM Follow-up Timeline: a Recovered KPI and a table of the program's children each with their latest MUAC and colour band, then one child's drill-down timeline — the per-visit MUAC climbing follow-up by follow-up out of red, through yellow, into green, ending recovered.
